Try to position this three-bone template a little forward. ## Copying and Positioning the Templates Now, can I make a relatively long three-bone template first and then directly put this finished three-bone template? The answer is no. If you directly create a relatively long three-bone template, it may be a bit crooked. If you just copy and paste it over a long strip, manually adjusting it becomes more troublesome. In 3D space, when we operate this template, it's often inaccurate, which may lead to penetrations with the three bones. After penetrations, we still need to manually adjust it. It's better to create a shorter one first, as shown in my video. If you copy all the strips, as long as there is no match, it may penetrate. Because the three bones are relatively thin, the method we use is to copy a relatively short piece first, then pull the bottom plate together, and start to simulate. This way, you can slowly simulate along the direction of the three bones. ### Finalizing the Three-Bone Structure Now, I have copied all the short three-bone panels and put them in place. Because the extension of the grid will follow the original rhythm, and since our three-bone rhythm is relatively large, we try to stretch it little by little. After selecting all the bottom plates, stretch them. If I stretch a whole one directly, its grid will transform seriously. At the beginning, this kind of rhythm is not obvious; it may be okay. However, when it comes to the later rhythm, if it's more obvious, it may have some more significant penetrations or transformations. So we press `Ctrl + Z` to go back to before. Not so much adjustment is better. Now we stretch it little by little. When doing this step, you may need a little patience. When making the scattered faces, we can use a tool first. Here we click the tool under the measurement tool, called the straight measurement clothing. This tool is used to measure the distance between the points on the clothing or the distance of a whole circle. Here, we can first click a point, then move the mouse to the point next to it, and click again. In this way, the distance between these two points will be automatically measured in the middle. After we have measured its length, we can start to draw this triangle. First of all, this edge, we can see in the attribute editor on the right side, its length is almost 430 mm. So we wait a moment, because we want to expand it. We set its length to half of it, which is about 215 mm. Use the multilayer tool to click, then move your mouse to the side, along the horizontal direction. We can refer to this smart guide line. When its length is about 215 mm, we start to draw, then move the mouse, and refer to this pink guide line to make a triangle that is equal to the one we just drew. Note that the highest point and the bottom point we created at the beginning are vertical. This way, we can expand it along the middle line into a flat triangle. Then we use the adjustment board tool to put this board a little next to it. Select the middle line, right-click, and select expand.
